needs.title: Large vehicle turning and stopping space

source_cards.front: How close may you stop to a school bus whose red lights are flashing?
source_cards.back: When a school bus is stopped with its red lights flashing, you must stop your vehicle no closer than twenty feet from the bus.

source_cards.front: Must you stop for a school bus with flashing red lights if its stop arm is folded?
source_cards.back: You must stop for a school bus showing flashing red lights even when its stop arm has not swung out.

source_cards.front: How far must you stop from a school bus with flashing red lights, and what is the sole exception?
source_cards.back: Upon seeing a stopped school bus with flashing red lights, you must stop at least twenty feet away unless you are traveling in the opposite direction on a divided highway.

source_cards.front: What triggers your duty to stop for a school bus: the stop arm or the red lights?
source_cards.back: The trigger for stopping at a school bus is the flashing red lights, not the stop arm, so a bus whose arm stays folded still requires you to stop at least twenty feet away.

needs.title: Motorcycle road position and visibility

source_cards.front: What does Minnesota law now allow a motorcycle to do between lanes, and what is your duty?
source_cards.back: In Minnesota a motorcycle may legally ride or pass in the space between your vehicle and a vehicle in the next lane, and you must not get in the way of its safe movement.

source_cards.front: Where will you most often see motorcycles sharing lanes, and where else may they pass?
source_cards.back: You will most often see motorcycle lane sharing at a stoplight as riders move up to the front, but riders may also pass slow traffic on your left or right while using part of your lane.

source_cards.front: Is a motorcycle riding between lanes breaking the law?
source_cards.back: A motorcycle sharing your lane or riding between lanes is acting legally, so the driver's duty is to leave it room rather than block it.

source_cards.front: What steps must someone who has never held a license anywhere complete?
source_cards.back: Someone who has never held a license anywhere must pass a written test and a vision test, get an instruction permit and then pass a road test.

source_cards.front: Which tests does that new resident take if the former license has expired?
source_cards.back: For that new resident, a former license expired less than one year means passing the written test, and one expired more than one year means passing both the written and road tests.

source_cards.front: Which tests must a newcomer from a country other than the U.S. or Canada pass?

source_cards.front: What should you do when you first get into the vehicle?
source_cards.back: When you get in, adjust your seat and mirrors, seat passengers where they do not block your view or interfere with driving, and buckle up and have every passenger do the same.

source_cards.front: Which items appear on the required equipment list?
source_cards.back: The required-equipment diagram lists wipers, safety glass, a rearview mirror, horn, plates with a plate light, two ways to brake, high and low beam headlights, turn signals, bumpers, seat belts, a muffler, and a red taillight with red reflectors and a stop light.

source_cards.front: Which mirrors do passenger vehicles and hauling pickups need?
source_cards.back: Passenger vehicles need rearview mirrors, and a vehicle with no view through a rear window, such as a rental moving truck, or a pickup used for hauling needs an extra side mirror.

needs.title: Passing and no-passing situations

source_cards.front: When may you leave the right side of a wide road?
source_cards.back: On roads of sufficient width you keep to the right side unless you are passing a vehicle going your way, the right side is closed for construction or repair, the road has three marked lanes, signs make it one-way, or you are moving over for a stopped authorized vehicle under the Move Over Law.

source_cards.front: When may you exceed the limit by ten miles per hour?
source_cards.back: On two-lane highways posted at fifty-five miles per hour or higher you may go up to ten miles per hour over the limit, but only while lawfully passing another vehicle.

source_cards.front: What must you do when passing a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing lights?
source_cards.back: You must slow down when approaching or passing a stopped emergency vehicle with flashing emergency lights, and breaking this rule adds a surcharge of at least twenty-five dollars to the speeding fine.

source_cards.front: What should you check before passing?
source_cards.back: Take extra care passing at night, in poor visibility or on slippery roads, and before passing make sure oncoming traffic is far enough away and that nobody behind you is starting to pass.

source_cards.front: How do you signal and return when passing?
source_cards.back: Signal left before moving out to pass and signal right after passing, then return to the right lane once the whole vehicle you passed shows in your rearview mirror.

source_cards.front: How soon must you be back in your lane after passing?
source_cards.back: After passing you must be back on the right side of the road before you come within one hundred feet of an oncoming vehicle.

source_cards.front: Where may you not pass?
source_cards.back: You may not pass where a No Passing Zone sign is posted or where a solid yellow line is on your side of the center line, and double solid yellow lines forbid passing in both directions.

source_cards.front: How do single and double solid yellow lines differ for passing?
source_cards.back: A single solid yellow line on your side bans passing for you, while a double solid yellow line bans passing for drivers in both directions.

source_cards.front: What should you do when another driver is passing you?
source_cards.back: Do not pass when you are about to meet an oncoming vehicle, and when someone is passing you, stay in your lane and do not speed up.

source_cards.front: When may you pass on the right?
source_cards.back: You may pass on the right only when it is safe and the vehicle ahead is turning or about to turn left, or the road has room for two or more lanes of moving traffic each way, or it is a one-way road wide enough for two or more lanes with nothing in the way.

source_cards.front: May you use the shoulder or a bike lane to pass on the right?
source_cards.back: A pass on the right must stay on the main roadway: using a bike lane, the shoulder or the unpaved edge to get around a vehicle is not allowed.

needs.title: Roundabout approach and movement

source_cards.front: What should you do as you approach a roundabout?
source_cards.back: As you approach a roundabout, slow down, pick your lane before entering if it has more than one lane, yield to pedestrians and bicyclists crossing, and watch for signs or markings that require or forbid certain moves.

source_cards.front: When may you enter a roundabout?
source_cards.back: Enter a roundabout only after yielding to vehicles already circulating and after all traffic coming from your left has cleared.

source_cards.front: How do you drive once inside a roundabout?
source_cards.back: Inside a roundabout drive counterclockwise to your exit and never stop, pass or change lanes.

source_cards.front: What do you do if an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in a roundabout?
source_cards.back: If an emergency vehicle approaches while you are in a roundabout, leave the roundabout right away and then pull over.

source_cards.front: Which vehicles may leave their lane in a roundabout?
source_cards.back: Any combination vehicle, or a vehicle over forty feet long or more than ten feet wide, may leave its lane as needed to get through a roundabout while watching other traffic.

source_cards.front: Who yields when two large vehicles go through a multi-lane roundabout together?
source_cards.back: Entering cars yield to cars already in the roundabout, but when two large vehicles go through a multi-lane roundabout side by side, the driver on the right yields to the one on the left, slowing or stopping if needed.

source_cards.front: Where do you wait when turning left on green with oncoming traffic?
source_cards.back: When waiting to turn left on a green light with traffic coming toward you, pull into the intersection until your body lines up with the curb line, and you may only get to turn once the light turns yellow.

source_cards.front: What should you watch for when turning right on red?
source_cards.back: When you turn right on red, watch for oncoming drivers turning left in front of you, since their green arrow may come on before your light turns green.

source_cards.front: What must you do whenever you turn on a red light?
source_cards.back: Whenever you turn on a red light, yield to traffic and pedestrians, and where a No Turn on Red sign is posted, wait for the green light.

needs.title: Turning paths and lanes

source_cards.front: What should you do when the car ahead signals a left turn?
source_cards.back: If the car ahead is signaling a left turn, slow down and get ready to stop.

source_cards.front: How do you make a left turn and where do you finish?
source_cards.back: For a left turn, check behind you and signal, move into the lane nearest the center line, or just right of the road's center if lanes are unmarked, look both ways, yield if needed, and finish in the first lane to the right of the center line.

source_cards.front: How do you make a right turn and where do you finish?
source_cards.back: For a right turn, check behind you and signal, move close to the right curb, look both ways, yield if needed, and finish in the lane next to the curb.

source_cards.front: Where do left and right turns finish, and how do you steer?
source_cards.back: A left turn ends in the first lane to the right of the center line, while a right turn ends in the lane next to the curb, and both use hand-over-hand steering.

source_cards.front: When may you turn right on a red light?
source_cards.back: Many intersections allow a right turn on red after a complete stop in the correct lane, unless a No Turn on Red sign is posted, and only after checking every direction for pedestrians and traffic.

source_cards.front: When is a left turn on red allowed?
source_cards.back: A left turn on red is allowed in certain cases only when turning from a one-way street onto another one-way street, after a complete stop and once the intersection is clear.

source_cards.front: How do the rules for right on red and left on red differ?
source_cards.back: A right turn on red is allowed at many intersections, but a left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, and both need a complete stop first.

source_cards.front: What should you watch for when turning right on red?
source_cards.back: When you turn right on red, watch for oncoming drivers turning left in front of you, since their green arrow may come on before your light turns green.

source_cards.front: May you cross both lanes in one motion at a J-turn?
source_cards.back: During the right turn at a J-turn you may cross both lanes into the left-turn lane in a single motion when it is safe, which shortens your time in the through lanes.

source_cards.front: What extra care does turning left onto a divided highway need?
source_cards.back: Turning left onto a divided highway follows the same steps as crossing it, and you must leave enough room that you do not slow oncoming traffic while you speed up.

source_cards.front: When may you use a lane other than the right-hand lane?
source_cards.back: You may use a lane other than the right-hand lane when passing, preparing a left turn at an intersection or into a driveway, preparing a left-side exit from an expressway, freeway or interstate, driving an authorized emergency vehicle, or following a traffic control device, a peace officer or work zone directions.

source_cards.front: How far before stopping does a school bus turn on yellow lights in slower zones?

source_cards.back: In a speed zone above thirty-five miles per hour, a school bus driver turns on the flashing yellow lights at least three hundred feet before the bus stops.

source_cards.back: Failing to stop for a school bus is a misdemeanor, and a conviction brings a fine of at least five hundred dollars and the loss of your driving privileges.

source_cards.front: When do you not have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights?
source_cards.back: On a divided roadway you do not have to stop for a school bus with flashing red lights that is on the other side of the divider.

source_cards.front: How long after an illegal school bus pass may an officer arrest you?
source_cards.back: An officer with probable cause to believe you illegally passed a stopped school bus may arrest you within four hours of the violation.

source_cards.back: The owner or lessee of a vehicle used to break the school bus stopping law is guilty of a petty misdemeanor unless they can prove someone else was driving, in which case the driver is charged.

source_cards.front: How do the penalties differ for the driver and the owner in a school bus violation?

source_cards.front: What must you do at a steady red light?
source_cards.back: A steady red light means stop: halt at the stop line, before the crosswalk or before entering the intersection, and wait for the light to change.

source_cards.front: What does a red arrow require?
source_cards.back: A red arrow means stop at the stop line, before the crosswalk or before the intersection, and you may go in the arrow's direction only when it turns green.

source_cards.front: How does a red arrow differ from a steady red light?
source_cards.back: A red arrow and a steady red light both require a full stop at the stop line, but the red arrow controls only the movement in its direction.

source_cards.front: What do white lines and yellow lines each separate?
source_cards.back: Pavement markings direct and regulate traffic, with white lines for traffic going the same way and yellow lines for traffic going opposite ways.

source_cards.front: What do white lines separate?
source_cards.back: White lines separate lanes of traffic moving in the same direction.

source_cards.front: What do white dashes and shorter, thicker white dashes mean?
source_cards.back: White dashed lines mean you may change lanes, while shorter, thicker white dashes mean the lane is ending.

source_cards.front: What does a single solid white line mean, and what else does it mark?
source_cards.back: A solid white line means you should not change lanes, and solid white lines also mark crosswalks, stop lines, parking stalls and the edges of the road.

source_cards.front: What do double solid white lines mean?
source_cards.back: Double solid white lines mean you must not change lanes.

source_cards.front: How does a single solid white line differ from double solid white lines?
source_cards.back: A single solid white line says you should not change lanes, while double solid white lines say you must not.

source_cards.front: Who may use the space marked by a solid white line with a bicycle symbol?
source_cards.back: A solid white line with a bicycle symbol marks space only for bicycles and electric-assist bicycles, and riders there must travel the same direction as the traffic beside them.

source_cards.front: What do yellow lines separate?
source_cards.back: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.

source_cards.front: What do a solid yellow line and yellow dashes mean for passing?
source_cards.back: A solid yellow line means you must not pass, while yellow dashes mean you may pass.

source_cards.front: Is passing in a no-passing zone legal?
source_cards.back: Passing in a no-passing zone is illegal, and a solid yellow line marks where you must not pass.

source_cards.front: Which marking do you follow when a solid yellow line and dashes run side by side?
source_cards.back: Where a solid yellow line runs on one side and dashes on the other, follow the marking on your own lane's side.

source_cards.front: What do double solid yellow lines mean for passing?
source_cards.back: Double solid yellow lines forbid passing no matter which side of them you are driving on.

source_cards.front: On a two-lane road with yellow dashes, who may pass?
source_cards.back: On a two-lane, two-way road divided by yellow dashes, drivers in either lane may pass, but where one side has a solid yellow line, drivers in that lane may not.

source_cards.front: May you cross two solid yellow lines to pass on a four-lane road?
source_cards.back: On a road with two lanes each way separated by two solid yellow lines, do not cross those lines to pass.

source_cards.front: Why are turn lanes separated from through lanes by solid white lines?
source_cards.back: Solid white lines separate turn lanes from through lanes to discourage lane changes close to the intersection.

source_cards.front: How is a center left-turn-only lane marked, and who may use it?
source_cards.back: A center left-turn-only lane between opposing traffic is marked by parallel solid and dashed yellow lines, sometimes with white arrows, and drivers from either direction may use it to turn left onto a road or driveway.

source_cards.front: When may you cross into a reversible lane?
source_cards.back: Reversible lanes, used to keep rush-hour traffic moving, are bounded by dashed double yellow lines that you may cross only when the overhead signal for the lane shows a green arrow or a sign allows it.

source_cards.front: How do center turn lane markings differ from reversible lane markings?
source_cards.back: A center turn lane is marked by parallel solid and dashed yellow lines, while a reversible lane is bounded by dashed double yellow lines that need a green overhead arrow or a sign before you cross.

source_cards.front: How are carpool lanes separated from other freeway lanes?
source_cards.back: Carpool lanes may be separated from other freeway lanes by combinations of white or yellow lines.

source_cards.front: Whose directions come first when an officer is directing traffic?
source_cards.back: When an officer is directing traffic, obey the officer's hand signals instead of the traffic signals, signs or pavement markings.

source_cards.front: Who may direct traffic, and whose signals take priority?
source_cards.back: Law enforcement officers, and on some occasions other individuals, direct traffic, and when an officer is present the officer's hand signals come before signals, signs and pavement markings.

source_cards.front: When may you turn right after stopping at a red light?
source_cards.back: After stopping for a red light you may turn right once the intersection is clear and traffic is allowed in that direction, unless a No Turn on Red sign tells you to wait for green.

source_cards.front: What does a red arrow require?
source_cards.back: A red arrow means stop at the stop line, before the crosswalk or before the intersection, and you may go in the arrow's direction only when it turns green.

source_cards.front: How does a red arrow differ from a steady red light?
source_cards.back: A red arrow and a steady red light both require a full stop at the stop line, but the red arrow controls only the movement in its direction.

source_cards.front: What must you do at a flashing red light?
source_cards.back: At a flashing red light, stop completely, yield to vehicles and pedestrians who got to the intersection before you, and continue when it is clear.

source_cards.front: How does a steady red light differ from a flashing red light?
source_cards.back: A steady red light holds you until the light changes, while a flashing red light works like a stop sign, letting you go after a full stop once the intersection is clear.

source_cards.front: What does a steady yellow light or arrow mean?
source_cards.back: A steady yellow light or arrow means the signal is about to turn red, so do not enter the intersection if you can stop safely, and otherwise go through with caution.

source_cards.front: What does a flashing yellow light or arrow mean?
source_cards.back: A flashing yellow light or arrow means go through with caution and yield to vehicles and pedestrians already in the intersection.

source_cards.front: Whom must you still yield to on a green light?
source_cards.back: On a green light you may cross once the intersection is clear, but you still yield to vehicles or pedestrians in it, to oncoming traffic when turning left, and to pedestrians crossing in front of you when turning either way.

source_cards.front: What does a green arrow mean?
source_cards.back: A green arrow means you may turn in its direction, and the turn should be protected from oncoming or crossing traffic.

source_cards.front: How does a green light differ from a green arrow when turning left?
source_cards.back: A green light lets you go but leaves you to yield to oncoming traffic on a left turn, while a green arrow gives you a turn that should be protected from oncoming or crossing traffic.

source_cards.front: What should pedestrians do when the Walk signal shows?
source_cards.back: Pedestrians must obey pedestrian signals, and when the Walk signal shows they should still check that crossing is safe, then may finish crossing once they have started.

source_cards.front: What does a steady downward green arrow over a lane mean?
source_cards.back: A steady downward green arrow over a lane means you may drive in that lane.

source_cards.front: How do a downward green arrow and a red X over a lane differ?
source_cards.back: A steady downward green arrow means you may use the lane, and a steady red X means you may not.

source_cards.front: What does a steady downward yellow arrow over a freeway lane mean?
source_cards.back: A steady downward yellow arrow over a freeway lane means that lane will close, so prepare to move safely into another lane.

source_cards.front: How do a steady yellow X and a steady downward yellow arrow differ?
source_cards.back: A steady yellow X and a steady downward yellow arrow both tell you to prepare to leave the lane, the first because a lane-control change is coming and the second because the freeway lane will close.

source_cards.front: What does a flashing downward yellow arrow over a freeway lane mean?
source_cards.back: A flashing downward yellow arrow over a freeway lane means you may use the lane, but with caution.

source_cards.front: How do a flashing yellow X and a flashing downward yellow arrow differ?
source_cards.back: A flashing yellow X lets you use the lane only for a left turn, while a flashing downward yellow arrow lets you drive in the freeway lane with caution.

source_cards.front: What are freeway ramp meters?
source_cards.back: Ramp meters are red, yellow and green signal lights on freeway entrance ramps that control the flow of merging traffic, working like intersection signals.

source_cards.front: How many cars may go on each green at a metered ramp?
source_cards.back: At a metered freeway ramp only one car may go on each green light, so drivers take turns entering the highway.
